skill.name: python-packaging
skill.description: Create distributable Python packages with modern project structure, pyproject.toml metadata, build steps, and publishing guidance.
skill.summary: Guide Python project structure, packaging metadata, builds, and publishing workflows for libraries and CLI tools.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are documentation examples, metadata links, or Markdown formatting rather than executable behavior. The confirmed risk is credential handling around ~/.pypirc, which can store PyPI publishing tokens. No prompt injection or malicious intent evidence was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.suggestion: Prefer PyPI trusted publishing or scoped environment tokens. Add guidance to restrict file permissions and never commit ~/.pypirc.

remediation.issue: Private index examples can affect dependency trust boundaries.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users to verify private index ownership and avoid global pip.conf changes unless their organization requires them.

content.value_statement: Python packaging has many moving parts, including metadata, build outputs, dependencies, and release checks. This skill gives concise patterns for packaging libraries and CLI tools for distribution.
actual_capabilities: Defines minimal and full project structures with a recommended src layout.
Shows modern pyproject.toml metadata, build system settings, dependencies, classifiers, and project URLs.
Explains CLI entry points for Click and argparse based tools.
Guides local builds for wheels and source distributions with validation steps.
Covers TestPyPI, PyPI, GitHub Actions publishing, and private index examples.
Includes README, MANIFEST.in, .gitignore, and publishing checklist templates.
limitations: It provides guidance and templates; it does not execute builds or publish packages by itself.
Examples use placeholder names, URLs, and tokens that must be replaced carefully.
It does not replace PyPA documentation for uncommon build backends or regulated environments.
Private package index guidance needs local security review before use.

use_cases.title: Package a New Library
use_cases.description: Create a clean source layout, project metadata, dependencies, and release checklist for a reusable Python library.

use_cases.title: Ship a Command-Line Tool
use_cases.description: Add entry points, choose a CLI pattern, and prepare installable distributions for a Python command-line application.

use_cases.title: Standardize Internal Releases
use_cases.description: Document build, TestPyPI, private index, and automation patterns for repeatable package releases.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Package Skeleton
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design a minimal Python package layout for my library. Include required files, metadata, and testing folders.

prompt_templates.title: Convert a Script to a CLI Package
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to turn my Python script into an installable CLI package. Recommend entry points, dependencies, and release steps.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a PyPI Release
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review my package for a PyPI release. Check metadata, build outputs, documentation, versioning, and TestPyPI validation.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Team Packaging Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design a repeatable packaging workflow for a team. Include private index use, CI publishing, tokens, and verification gates.

output_examples.input: Create a package layout for a small utility library.
output: Recommended src layout with project metadata, README, license, tests, and development dependency groups.
Build and validation steps for creating a wheel and source distribution.
Release checklist covering version, changelog, metadata, and clean environment installation.

output_examples.input: Package a command-line tool for installation.
output: Entry point strategy for the command name and module function.
Dependency and optional dependency guidance for development and testing.
Checks for local installation, command invocation, and distribution validation.

output_examples.input: Plan a secure package publishing process.
output: Recommended TestPyPI trial release before public publishing.
Credential handling notes for scoped tokens or trusted publishing.
Automation review points for build, package check, upload, and post-release verification.

best_practices: Use a src layout and pyproject.toml for new packages.
Build and test wheels in a clean environment before release.
Use scoped publishing tokens or trusted publishing, and keep credentials outside repositories.
anti_patterns: Copying placeholder metadata or URLs into a real package without review.
Publishing directly to PyPI before testing on TestPyPI or a clean install.
Storing long-lived repository tokens in shared files or committed configuration.

faq.question: Does this skill create package files automatically?
faq.answer: It gives instructions and templates. The AI assistant can apply them when you provide project files.

faq.question: Does it support pyproject.toml?
faq.answer: Yes. The playbook focuses on modern pyproject.toml metadata, build systems, dependencies, and tool configuration.

faq.question: Can it help with CLI tools?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers entry points and examples for Click and argparse based command-line packages.

faq.question: Can it publish my package to PyPI?
faq.answer: It explains the release process, but publishing still requires your credentials, review, and explicit action.

faq.question: Does it cover private package indexes?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes private index examples that should be adapted to your organization security policy.

faq.question: Is this a replacement for PyPA documentation?
faq.answer: No. It is a practical guide for common workflows and should be checked against official PyPA guidance for edge cases.
